purpose: These are the questions a reviewer must answer before the site's numbers can reasonably drive a decision. Each has: what we HAVE (with the source), what we DO NOT HAVE, how to discover the missing part, and what decision it blocks. A question with a complete answer is marked answered; nothing here is inferred.

legend.have: the evidence actually held in the repository or read from an official source this session
legend.missing: what is not held, stated precisely
legend.discovery: a concrete, checkable way to obtain it
legend.blocks: the suggestion ids that may not proceed until this is answered

questions.question: Where can a timestamped opening and closing price be obtained, for which seasons and markets, and under what licence?
questions.have: One price per market in the schedules feed with no sampling time (7,103 games). A separate early snapshot for 2021 with 272 games quoted (n=67 matched to a close).
questions.missing: A publisher that states when each price was taken. No licence terms for redistribution are held.
questions.discovery: Ask each candidate archive for a sample with timestamps; verify two known closes independently; record the licence in data/sources.json before ingesting.

questions.question: How current must the results feed be for a decision, and who runs the refresh?
questions.have: Weekly scheduled workflows exist and are green on main. Official Week 9 finals read from NFL.com; Week 10 Thursday result read from NFL.com.
questions.missing: A defined freshness SLA and an automated official reconciliation step.
questions.discovery: Decide the maximum acceptable lag (e.g. 24h after the last game), then encode it as a check that fails the build when exceeded.

questions.question: Is the rating model meant to beat the closing line, or only to describe a team?
questions.have: Walk-forward error worse than the market in all four evaluated seasons; ATS win rate on its own side 43.8%-48.9%.
questions.missing: An explicit objective. Both are legitimate; publishing both without choosing invites misreading.
questions.discovery: State the objective in one sentence on the methods page and make the gate test that objective.

questions.question: What price is actually available to the account, and is it the same price the model is scored against?
questions.have: Feed prices for 73.2% of spread legs; no account, venue, limit or jurisdiction is held or stated anywhere.
questions.missing: Verified executable prices and stake limits. Without them a positive-EV number is hypothetical.
questions.discovery: Record the venue, the observed price at a stated time, and the maximum stake for a sample of bets, and re-price the model against that.

questions.question: Can the build reach the third-party release assets it depends on for snap counts and depth charts?
questions.have: No from this sandbox (TLS reset on all four feeds). Yes from a GitHub runner: the repository's existing fetch workflow has succeeded repeatedly.
questions.missing: A committed run of THIS hub's fetch step inside CI.
questions.discovery: Add the workflow, dispatch it once, and confirm the manifest hashes land in data/inputs/manifest.json.
questions.answer: Yes on CI, no locally; the workflow is the discovery mechanism.

questions.question: What weighting makes 'depth lost' comparable across positions and clubs?
questions.have: 66 players Out across 28 clubs in the official Week 10 report; per-club counts by status.
questions.missing: Any official depth rank (the NFL publishes none machine-readable) and an agreed weighting.
questions.discovery: Pre-register the formula in this file, then evaluate it on a holdout season before it enters any strategy.

questions.question: Is there any prop-price history available at all, and at what cost?
questions.have: Measured correlations with large n (e.g. receptions vs yards r=0.80, n=45,315).
questions.missing: Every historical prop price. n=0 priced prop bets.
questions.discovery: Request a sample of prop prices for one week from a provider; if none is obtainable, retire the prop family from the competition rather than leaving it looking merely untested.

questions.question: Would you rather have a lower statistical bar or a longer wait?
questions.have: A sample floor of n>=300 graded / n>=100 priced that no strategy currently meets.
questions.missing: A decision on whether the floor is right, given that most families have 9 seasons of data at most.
questions.discovery: Compute the power curve for the observed effect sizes and choose the floor from the power analysis, not from impatience.

questions.question: Is the competition funded, and if so by whom, in what currency, with what rules?
questions.have: Three published tiers; prize_pool null; status UNFUNDED.
questions.missing: Any funding, sponsor, or payment mechanism, and any legal review of paying contest participants.
questions.discovery: Either name a funded pool and its rules, or drop the word reward.

questions.question: What is the minimum evidence before a strategy may be called live, and who signs it off?
questions.have: Ten gates, six demotion triggers, two promotion rules, all published and computed in code.
questions.missing: A named accountable owner and a tested transition (no strategy has ever been live, so no demotion has ever fired).
questions.discovery: Run one strategy through SIMULATED live and paper states on historical data to prove the transition code works before it matters.

questions.question: Does the same-game correlation structure hold across positions and seasons, or is one number being over-generalised?
questions.have: Pooled coefficients with confidence intervals; e.g. QB yards vs WR1 yards r=0.55 (n=5,893, CI 0.533-0.569).
questions.missing: Stability by season and by team. A pooled r can hide a regime change.
questions.discovery: Publish the coefficient by season with its own n and interval; a signal that only holds in one era is a warning, not an edge.
questions.answer: Partially: pooled values are measured and stable in sign, but a per-season stability table is not yet published.

questions.question: Is the official injury report the right input for a pre-kickoff decision, given that statuses change on Saturday and again before kickoff?
questions.have: The Week 10 report as read on 2026-11-14, with practice and game status per player.
questions.missing: A defined snapshot time for the report used as a feature, and confirmation of how quickly statuses change.
questions.discovery: Capture the report at a fixed clock time each week (e.g. Saturday 21:00 UTC) and store the capture time as part of the record.

questions.question: Should the site publish a single composite score, or only the separate signal and staking columns?
questions.have: Signal and staking are published separately and the ranking uses signal first.
questions.missing: A decision on whether a composite (currently 0.6 signal / 0.4 staking) helps or obscures.
questions.discovery: Test whether the composite changes the ranking under reasonable weight changes; if it does, it is not a summary, it is an opinion.

questions.question: What does a reviewer do with a 'flagged' item - is it a request to fix, or a note to self?
questions.have: A flagged page with every unverifiable value and its reason.
questions.missing: A workflow that assigns an owner and a state to each flag.
questions.discovery: Add an owner and a state to every flag row, mirroring the suggestions register, and confirm the fix in the next build.
